title: Esh Hotel and Spa / FAMM Arquitectura + Sulkin Askenazi
text:
Esh Hotel and Spa / FAMM Arquitectura + Sulkin Askenazi

ESH Hotel & Spa is a 29-key hospitality development located on a sloping site in Nosara, Costa Rica. The project began with a central challenge: how to create a destination hotel on a property with limited long-distance views. Rather than organizing the experience around a distant panorama, the design constructs an internal landscape from the site itself. Preserved trees, a natural creek, planted courtyards, water, and shaded outdoor spaces become the primary points of orientation throughout the hotel.

title: Paquetá House / Zebulun Arquitetura
text:
Paquetá House / Zebulun Arquitetura

The site is surrounded by four adjacent lots, with no direct view of the street. The design therefore stems from the intention to expand the house’s program while ensuring environmental quality and comfort for all rooms.

title: Feliza Bursztyn School / AR-AR (Martínez Arquitectura)
text:
Feliza Bursztyn School / AR-AR (Martínez Arquitectura)

The Feliza Bursztyn School is conceived as an urban link that integrates, through its design, the neighborhood dynamics and the serenity of a landscaped public space in Bogotá.

title: Coral Barn Alvorada House / Nildo José Arquitetos
text:
Coral Barn Alvorada House / Nildo José Arquitetos

Coral, the official paint and sponsor of CASACOR São Paulo, alongside Nildo José and NJ+ Arquitetura, in their seventh participation in the event, presents Casa Coral Celeiro Alvorada, a tribute to Brazil's countryside heritage. The name of the space stems from the idea of "celar" (to seal or keep safe), guarding what matters, and also from Parque da Água Branca itself, which has its origins linked to agriculture and agribusiness and is celebrating 30 years since its landmark designation. Connected to this history and reinforced by this edition's theme, "Mind and Heart," Coral continues the narrative that began last year, in a project that addresses the relationship between memory, affection, and permanence. The architecture, interior design, and landscaping exhibition will run from June 2 to August 9 at Parque da Água Branca in São Paulo.

title: Helix Residence / SAOTA
text:
Helix Residence / SAOTA

Set in the Los Angeles Bird Streets above Sunset Boulevard, this private residence draws on the city's modernist tradition of hillside living, where architecture and landscape merge to celebrate light, views, and openness. The design engages directly with its steep topography, balancing privacy with panoramic connections to the city below.

title: The XVII Spanish Biennial of Architecture and Urbanism (BEAU) opens its first international tour in Tokyo
text:
The XVII Spanish Biennial of Architecture and Urbanism (BEAU) opens its first international tour in Tokyo

The exhibition of the 17th Spanish Biennial of Architecture and Urbanism (BEAU) will arrive at the Embassy of Spain in Tokyo, Japan, on September 4, marking its first international venue following its tour through Ponferrada, La Palma, and Avilés. Curated by Ander Bados and Miguel Ramón under the title Flujos Comunes (Common Flows), Tokyo will be the penultimate stop of this traveling exhibition, designed to promote the talent, diversity, and innovative capacity of Spanish architecture and urbanism on an international scale.

title: BIAU | The XIV Ibero-American Biennial of Architecture and Urbanism announces the 174 selected projects | Brasilia 2026
text:
BIAU | The XIV Ibero-American Biennial of Architecture and Urbanism announces the 174 selected projects | Brasilia 2026

The XIV Ibero-American Biennial of Architecture and Urbanism (BIAU) announces the selected projects
A total of 174 projects have been selected from the 711 proposals submitted in the Works and Publications category; the finalists will be announced in September. Under the theme "Caring for Life," the Biennial is conceived as a space for critical reflection on contemporary territorial transformations, structured around four thematic axes: water, vegetation, communities, and housing. The XIV BIAU will take place in Brasília from November 3 to 7.

title: Tiger Track Ecolodge / Building Bureau
text:
Tiger Track Ecolodge / Building Bureau

The Tiger Track Ecolodge is a model for wildlife tourism and a demonstration of contemporary earth construction in Bardiya, Nepal. Located in the Khata Corridor between Bardiya National Park and India's Katarniaghat Wildlife Sanctuary, the project responds to two interrelated pressures: increasing human-wildlife conflict and the erosion of local building traditions. Tourism revenue supports a Single Women's Wildlife Victim Fund and the Community-Based Anti-Poaching Unit (CBAPU), whose Rapid Response Team is based at the lodge. Architecturally, the project reinterprets the low, mud-plastered walls and simple gable roofs of the indigenous Tharu settlements while challenging the assumption that earth is temporary, weak, or incompatible with modern development.

title: Medellín Design Fair
text:
Medellín Design Fair

La Feria De Diseño Medellín, powered by idd cologne, is a professional platform that connects Latin American design with international markets. From September 10 to 12, 2026, it will bring together brands, architects, interior designers, buyers, developers, distributors, and industry leaders at Plaza Mayor Medellín, focusing on furniture, lighting, kitchens, architecture, interior design, wellness, and decoration.

Its agenda integrates exhibitions, knowledge sharing, and business opportunities for Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: Val d'Oust Cultural Center / Atelier 56S
text:
Val d'Oust Cultural Center / Atelier 56S

The Val d'Oust Cultural Center stands as a key public facility at the intersection of the church square, Jules Ferry Street, and the landscaped public garden. The project forms part of a broader strategy to enhance public spaces and strengthen pedestrian connections throughout the town.

title: Has Architecture Ever Been Entirely Human? Beatriz Colomina and Mark Wigley on the Microbial Nature of Architecture
text:
Has Architecture Ever Been Entirely Human? Beatriz Colomina and Mark Wigley on the Microbial Nature of Architecture

Architecture has long been understood as a discipline created by humans and for humans. But in We the Bacteria: Notes Toward Biotic Architecture, Beatriz Colomina and Mark Wigley challenge that assumption, arguing that "microbes invented architecture." From this premise unfolds an alternative history of architecture that shifts the focus away from human exceptionalism and toward the microorganisms that have shaped life, environments, and the built world for billions of years.

title: Rooms That Appear: Sliding Partitions and Conditional Domestic Space
text:
Rooms That Appear: Sliding Partitions and Conditional Domestic Space

Sliding doors are often discussed through efficiency. They save the swing radius of a conventional door, allow compact rooms to function more easily, and help small apartments borrow a few extra centimeters of usable space. Yet in many interiors, their more interesting role is not only spatial economy. Sliding partitions transform the reading of the room itself. A bedroom, study, guest room, dining area, or workspace can appear when a panel is closed, disappear when it is opened, and remain ambiguous when the boundary is translucent or partial.

title: Chengdu Pavilion / IwamotoScott Architecture
text:
Chengdu Pavilion / IwamotoScott Architecture

The Chengdu pavilion was commissioned as an exhibition pavilion with a project brief seeking a decidedly future-forward design. It serves both as an iconic symbol of the ethos and purpose of the adjacent future-facing urban expansion currently underway and as an information center for the public to learn about this large new master-planned district called the Chengdu Future Science and Technology City now in development and construction in the Sichuan Province.

title: MAD’s Shenzhen Bay Culture Square and Dorte Mandrup’s PLACE Exhibition: This Week’s Review
text:
MAD’s Shenzhen Bay Culture Square and Dorte Mandrup’s PLACE Exhibition: This Week’s Review

This week, architecture's relationship with culture took center stage through exhibitions, public projects, and new cultural infrastructure that extend architectural discourse beyond the building itself. While major exhibitions from Australia, Shanghai, Barcelona, and Copenhagen examined themes of housing, landscape, and place through research and design, newly unveiled projects in China and Italy demonstrate how museums, performance venues, and mixed-use projects are increasingly conceived as open public landscapes rather than isolated institutions, while new exhibitions and construction milestones reflect ongoing experimentation in adaptive reuse, context-responsive design, and flexible urban environments.

title: Masseria Ficazzella / Valari Studio
text:
Masseria Ficazzella / Valari Studio

Nestled in the Fasano countryside among olive trees and distant views of the Adriatic, Masseria Ficazzella is a restoration by Valari Studio that reimagines a historic Puglian farmhouse as a contemporary private home. Designed for a young, non-Italian family, the project balances architectural authenticity, domestic comfort, and a close relationship with the landscape.

title: Grand Paris Express Advances Urban Renewal Through 68 Architect-Designed Stations
text:
Grand Paris Express Advances Urban Renewal Through 68 Architect-Designed Stations

The Grand Paris Express project consists of 200 kilometers of new, fully automated metro lines, 68 new stations, and four new orbital lines (15, 16, 17, and 18), in addition to the extension of Line 14. The network is being delivered in phases between 2024 and 2031: Line 14's 8 stations are fully operational following its 2024 extension, Line 18 is the most advanced of the new lines, with testing underway ahead of its first opening, and civil engineering is largely complete on many sections, with tracks, systems, architectural fit-out, and testing now progressing station by station. Each of the 68 stations is assigned to a specific architect or architectural team, sometimes in collaboration with landscape architects for above-ground elements.

title: Workmanship and Imperfection: 10 Projects Between Hand and Machine
text:
Workmanship and Imperfection: 10 Projects Between Hand and Machine

In 1968, the furniture designer and RCA professor David Pye published The Nature and Art of Workmanship, a book built around a distinction between "workmanship of risk" and the "workmanship of certainty." Pye was not writing about architecture, and despite how the phrase gets used today, he was not really writing about hands versus machines either. He pointed out that a printing press, entirely mechanical, still depends on someone judging the ink and the register, while a woodturner working a lathe by hand can follow a template closely enough that almost nothing is left to chance.

title: The Plinth House / Cambra Buró
text:
The Plinth House / Cambra Buró

The Plinth House is a 3,000 sqm private villa on the coast of Abu Alhusaniya, Kuwait, completed in 2025. Designed by Cambra Buró under a full architectural, interior, and landscape scope, the house is structured as a dialogue between restraint and expression: a sculpted travertine plinth anchors the building to the ground, while a minimal, calm upper volume rests above it, deliberately understated in contrast to the base.

title: Entwined Wall Residence / IGArchitects
text:
Entwined Wall Residence / IGArchitects

This project is the renovation of a single floor within a commercial tenant building into a restaurant. Rather than dividing the program into a conventional relationship of front-of-house and back-of-house, the design explores how the various functions of the restaurant can be encompassed and gently interconnected through a single continuous wall.

title: aa Market / Vari Architects
text:
aa Market / Vari Architects

aa market is a rooftop lifestyle market initiated, designed, and operated by vari architects in Chongqing. Rather than beginning as a conventional commercial commission, the project grew out of the architects' own daily needs. Located above their studio, it was first imagined as a place where the team, friends, and the surrounding community could eat, drink tea, meet, pause, and spend time together. From this small-scale spatial practice, the project gradually developed into an attempt to reactivate an overlooked rooftop within an industrial park and transform it into a new public interface for everyday urban life.

title: Brutalist Penthouse  / Barde + vanVoltt
text:
Brutalist Penthouse / Barde + vanVoltt

Located in the Escandón neighborhood of Mexico City, this 300-square-meter penthouse renovation by Barde vanVoltt reinterprets brutalist architecture through warmth, craftsmanship, and domestic comfort. Designed for two creative professionals, the project transforms an existing rooftop apartment into a calm sanctuary above one of the city's most vibrant districts.

title: Praça House / Felipe Hess Arquitetos
text:
Praça House / Felipe Hess Arquitetos

Implanted on a narrow and deep plot of 10 x 60 meters in Jardim Paulistano, Casa Praça is organized into three blocks interspersed with patios. This configuration takes advantage of the lot's geometry to distribute the spaces functionally and create open areas that enhance the entry of natural light and encourage social interaction.

title: PH Juana / Estudio NU
text:
PH Juana / Estudio NU

PH Juana proposes a space where the existing and the new coexist to give rise to a fresh reinterpretation of contemporary living.

title: HD House / Desvão Atelier
text:
HD House / Desvão Atelier

Casa HD is located within a residential enclave between Sesimbra and the village of Azeitão, occupying a trapezoidal plot bounded by the access road to the east and adjacent buildings to the north and south. While the topography is relatively gentle, the existing slope was leveraged to raise the construction one metre above street level, eliminating the need for major earthworks and enhancing visual and spatial autonomy. Situated near the Arrábida Natural Park, the site benefits from a striking natural backdrop dominated by the surrounding mountain range. The landscape is characterized by cork oaks, holm oaks, and scattered low vegetation, typical of the Portuguese montado ecosystem.
